summary: Robert Needham Cust (1821–1909) worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Eton College (~1834–1840) and Haileybury and Imperial Service College (~1840–1842), and held a post in the Bengal Civil Service (~1843–1867).

Robert P. Goldman (b. 1942) is an Indologist who studied at Columbia University (~1960–1964) and the University of Pennsylvania (~1964–1971) under Shivaram Dattatray Joshi. He held a post at the University of California, Berkeley from ~1971.

Robert S. Nelson (b. 1947) is an art historian and archaeologist. He studied at Rice University (~1965–1969) and New York University (~1972–1978), and held professorial posts at the University of Chicago (~1974–2005) and Yale University (~2005–2021).
Robert Warren Clark works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his studies under doctoral supervisor Karen C. Lang and adviser K. L. Seshagiri Rao.
Robert Zimmermann (1874–1931) was an Indologist. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1910–1913) and held an academic post at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai (~1914–1930).

Robin Coningham (b. 1965) works in archaeology and Indology. He studied at King's College (1985–1994) and the University of Cambridge (~1989–1994), later holding posts at the University of Bradford (~1994–2005) and Durham University (2005).
Roderick Chisholm (1916–1999) was a philosopher who studied at Harvard University (~1938–1942). He held academic posts at Brown University (~1947–1995) and the University of Massachusetts Amherst.

Roderick S. Bucknell (1937–2026) worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He held a long-term post at the University of Queensland (~1976–2002), where he served as an Associate Professor from ~1990 to 2002.

Roderick Whitfield (b. 1937) is a scholar of archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the British Museum (attested 1986) and SOAS University of London, where he was attested as professor emeritus in 2011.

Roger R. Jackson (b. 1950) works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He studied at Wesleyan University and the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, later holding posts at Carleton College (~1989–2016).

Roger T. Ames (b. 1947) is a philosopher and Sinologist. After studying at the University of British Columbia and National Taiwan University, he held posts at the University of Hawaii (~1978–2016) and Peking University (~2016).
Roland Steiner is a scholar of Indology and Tibetology who studied under Michael Hahn. He held a post as Assistant Professor at the University of Marburg (attested 2002).

Roland Wenzlhuemer (b. 1976) is a historian who studied at the University of Salzburg (~1996–2002). He held academic posts at Heidelberg University (~2008–2017) and Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~2017).

Rolf Alfred Stein (1911–1999) worked in Tibetology and Sinology, studying under Paul Pelliot and Henri Maspero. He held posts at INALCO (~1948–1951), École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1951–1975), and the Collège de France (1965–1981).

Rolf Scheuermann is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Vienna (attested 2010) under MA supervisor Helmut Tauscher and traditional teacher Khenpo Chodrak Tenphel.

Romila Thapar (b. 1931) is an Indian historian. She studied at Panjab University and the University of London under Arthur Llewellyn Basham, later holding posts at the University of Delhi (~1963–1970) and Jawaharlal Nehru University (attested 2001).
Ron Garry is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers Lama Tharchin Rinpoche and Tulku Thubten Rinpoche.
Ron Leifer (1932–2017) was a scholar in Buddhist studies. He studied under Agehananda Bharati in 1964 and with traditional teacher Khenpo Karthar Rinpoche from ~1976 to 2017.

Ronald D. Schwartz works in Tibetology and sociology. In 1998, he was attested as Professor of Sociology at Memorial University of Newfoundland and as an Honorary Research Fellow at the University of Hong Kong.

Ronald E. Purser (b. 1956) works in religious studies, philosophy, and management. He studied under Koshin Ogui in 1985 and held posts at Loyola University Chicago (~1989–1995) and San Francisco State University (~1995).
